sections.name: Document Upload Classification & State Machine
sections.title: Labelling and upload status checks
sections.what: Checks sample file names for each label and checks that an example upload moves from idle to completed in order.
sections.why: Protects the labels users depend on and gives a basic check of status values.
sections.watch_out: One test expects a file named unknown_scan to be labelled imaging, which relies on the scan keyword being checked before others. Changing the rule order can break it.

summary: Tests the rules that label uploaded files by document type and checks a simple example of how upload status changes.
purpose: Makes sure file names are sorted into the right document categories, such as lab report or prescription, so uploads get the right label.
why: Document labels affect how the app later processes and shows files, so wrong labels would show users the wrong information.
how: The file defines its own copy of the classification rules, then checks sample file names against expected categories. A second group of tests checks example status values with no real upload code involved.
inputs: Sample file names and example status objects written in the test.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each test case, shown by the test runner.
risks: The tests do not import the real classification function from use-upload.ts. They test a copy, so the real code can change and the tests still pass. The status tests check fixed example values and do not test real behavior.
debug: If a file is labelled wrongly in the app, first check the real function in use-upload.ts, then compare it with the copy here. If tests pass but uploads fail, the tests are not covering the real code.
